relationships.description: Weathered phreatic aquifer overlies fractured aquifer which overlies massive impervious base defining lower limit of movement
Partial Cauvery coverage in outer peripheral wards forces borewell tanker dependence causing overexploitation and scarcity
Eastern high-yield fractured zones with deep levels thick weathered cover low rainfall and lacking piped supply compact upon dewatering producing InSAR subsidence
Phase 3 elevated double-decker corridors founded in PGC granite-gneiss require pier-specific investigation and precast plus long-span steel solutions
KML LineString network spatially represents BWSSB distribution referenced for recharge siting flood and scarcity planning but without hydraulic attributes
Cascading lake filling desilting defunct-well and park percolation interventions target Aquifer-I shallow and Aquifer-II fractured storage to close deficit
Phase 3 corridors follow existing Outer Ring Road (C1 circular) and Magadi radial road (C2); viaduct centred on road median with soffit >=5.5 m
C1 and C2 merge vertically at Sumanahalli Cross: C2 upper, C1 lower; road viaduct avoids station horizontally; clearance shortfall requires structural mitigation
Borehole program underpins pile vs raft selection per pier; deep-soil zones flagged for detailed design
Water/communication utilities buried along road edge conflict with pier/borehole positions; trial 2.5 m pits and opposite-side siting required
Fresh granite-gneiss bedrock provides end-bearing for piles socketed 1-3 m into fresh rock; allowable bearing via IS 12070/RMR/core strength
In normal conditions Nagarbhavi feeds JP Nagar 4th Phase to Vinayaka Layout; BEL Circle feeds Vinayaka Layout to Kempapura; either can feed full Corridor 1 in emergency.
BEL Circle RSS backs up KHB Colony RSS for Corridor 2 emergency feed; normal Corridor 2 feed from KHB Colony; integration planned at Sumanahalli station.
First BMRCL physical interconnection enables through-service between Airport Line (Phase-2B) and Phase-3 Corridor-1 via Gateway device; requires same-manufacturer (Alstom) CBTC.
Main depot supports both corridors; GoA4 movement limited to third-rail areas with stinger/manual handling in inspection/workshop.
Satellite facility adds night stabling and minor inspection/cleaning capacity for Corridor 1 via turnout connection.

Herohalli Lake in Cauvery basin near alignment; Hebbal and Nagavara Lakes in South Pennar basin; all in valley/lake system requiring careful construction/operation handling for stormwater and ecology.

BWSSB piped network coexists with metro corridor road traffic/pollution zone; joint construction interface and utility diversion risk to be managed, but line-level crossings not resolved in this batch.
Metro alignment (Line 3-2 southern end) lies 7.05-7.1 km north of Bannerghatta National Park boundary; park is nearest legally designated protected area, all KBAs >7 km.
Cubbon Park (~5 km) and Lalbagh (~3.8 km) are centrally located botanical urban green lungs distant from proposed alignment but indicate urban ecological context.
Residual soils mantle granitic gneiss bedrock; district elevations 850-950 m AMSL on Deccan Plateau pediplain sloping south-southeast.
Listed Reserved/Protected Forests (e.g., Doresanipalya 3.5 km, Kadugodi 4.5 km) managed under Indian Forest Act 1927, not Wildlife Protection Act, and assessed as not critical habitat.

BWSSB water-supply line network (97827 features) underlies same BMA urban fabric as metro alignments and resettlement water-access permits; coordination between BMRCL and BWSSB required for relocation sites.
